nodes.title: Isoperimetric inequality

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $s$ be a bounded subset of the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ with diameter $\operatorname{diam} s$. Then there is a point $c \in \mathbb{R}^n$ such that $s$ is contained in the closed ball with center $c$ and radius $\sqrt{n / (2(n + 1))} \cdot \operatorname{diam} s$.
nodes.title: Jung's theorem

nodes.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be finite sets of points in $\mathbb{R}^d$. Then $A$ and $B$ are strictly separated by a hyperplane, that is, there are a nonzero vector $w \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and a real number $\beta$ with $\langle w, a \rangle < \beta$ for all $a \in A$ and $\beta < \langle w, c \rangle$ for all $c \in B$, if and only if for every set $C \subseteq A \cup B$ of at most $d + 2$ points, the sets $A \cap C$ and…
nodes.title: Kirchberger's theorem

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $p_1, \dots, p_n$ be points of $\mathbb{R}^d$, not necessarily distinct. Then some point $x$ in the convex hull of $\{p_1, \dots, p_n\}$ has at least $n/(d+1)$ of the points in every closed halfspace containing it: for all $v \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and $t \in \mathbb{R}$ with $\langle v, x \rangle \le t$, the number of indices $i$ with $\langle v, p_i \rangle \le t$ is at least $n/(d+1)$.
nodes.title: Rado's centerpoint theorem

nodes.summary: Let $d, r$ be natural numbers with $r \ge 1$ and let $N = (d+1)(r-1)+1$. For any points $p_1, \dots, p_N$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$, not necessarily distinct, there are pairwise disjoint sets $P_1, \dots, P_r \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ whose union is $\{1, \dots, N\}$ and a point $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ that lies in the convex hull of $\{p_i : i \in P_j\}$ for every $j$.
nodes.title: Tverberg's theorem

nodes.summary: Let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ be a compact set homeomorphic to the closed unit ball. Suppose that for every nonzero continuous linear functional $F : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}$ and every real $c$ such that the plane $\{x : F(x) = c\}$ meets the interior of $K$, the intersection of this plane with the boundary (frontier) of $K$ is homeomorphic to the unit circle. Then $K$ is convex.
nodes.title: Ulam's flat-sections problem in dimension three

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
